questions.q: What is the target variable for the SR-5 model?
options: The forward 5-day return, expressed as a cross-sectional rank
questions.explain: The model predicts the forward 5-day return, expressed as a forward 5-day cross-sectional rank across the 11 sectors.

questions.q: Which feature directly captures the volatility-regime conditioning idea central to the SR-5 hypothesis?
questions.explain: vix_regime encodes the VIX level and its term-structure slope, which is how the strategy conditions the reversal signal on fear/calm regimes.

questions.q: Why is every feature cross-sectionally z-scored rather than used at its raw, absolute level?
options: Raw levels are illegal to use in backtests
Z-scoring makes the model train faster
A relative ranking across the 11 sectors stays meaningful across very different regimes, while an absolute level (like '18% volatility') does not
Ridge regression cannot accept un-scaled inputs of any kind
questions.explain: Cross-sectional z-scoring means the model sees relative standing among sectors that day, which is comparable whether the regime is a crisis or a calm period.

questions.q: What problem does the 5-day embargo between the feature window and the target window prevent?
options: Leakage, where overlapping windows let the model see information it couldn't have known at decision time
questions.explain: Because the target is a forward 5-day return, feature and target windows can overlap without a deliberate gap; the embargo purges that overlap to prevent leakage.

questions.q: cross_sectional_z(frame) in the feature engineering code computes the z-score of each day's values relative to what?
options: The mean and standard deviation across the 11 sectors on that same day
The prior year's average value for that sector
questions.explain: cross_sectional_z subtracts the row-wise (across-sector) mean and divides by the row-wise standard deviation — a same-day, cross-sector normalization.
